Rashi on Gittin 15a:11:1.english: One line - [The] first line, in which [are] the name of the man, the woman, and the date:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רב חסדא כו' - לאו לפרושי מתני' אתא ולאוקומי מתני' בהכי, אלא סברא דידיה מוסיף ואמר רבותא: דאפי' שנים מן השוק מעידין שהן מכירין יד עד חתימת השני שלא העיד השליח עליו — פסול:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:12:1.english: Rav Chisda said, etc. - He did not come to explain the Mishnah or to establish the Mishnah as [referring to] this [case]; rather, he adds his own reasoning and states a novel point: that even if two [people] from the marketplace testify that they recognize the handwriting of the second witness, regarding whom the agent did not testify, it is invalid:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:13:1.english: Ratification of the bill of divorce - This means witnesses who testify regarding the signature of the witnesses:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:13:2.english: The rabbinic decree - [This refers to] the testimony of the agent, whom the Sages believed like two [witnesses]:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:14:1.hebrew: מי איכא מידי דאילו אמר חד כשר - אם היה אומר השליח "אני מכירם", כשר, ואפילו לא אמר "בפני נחתם", דהכי אמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל גיטין דף ג.), דכי אמר "יודע אני" נמי מהימן, בשמעתא קמייתא:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:14:1.english: Is there anything where if one said [so], it is valid - If the agent had said, "I recognize them," it is valid, even if he did not say, "It was signed in my presence," for so we say in the first chapter (above, Gittin 3a), that when he says, "I know [their signatures]," he is also believed, in the first sugya:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:1:1.english: My brooch [kevinati] - Nosche in Old French [a brooch or clasp]:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:1:2.hebrew: והיא בי"ב מנה - כך היתה שוה:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:1:2.english: And it [is] twelve maneh - That is how much it was worth:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:1:3.hebrew: תקברם אמם - קללה היא, כלומר: לא יעלו על לב ולא יזכרו בבית המדרש לראיה, לפי שרשעים היו, שהיו מקיימין קוצים בכרם, ולר"א כלאים נינהו; ולא נלמד מהן ראיה, לפי שלא דקדקנו בהן איך היתה אותה צואה, שמתוך שהיו רשעים לא הוזכרו בבהמ"ד:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:1:3.english: May their mother bury them - [This] is a curse, meaning: may they not come to mind and may they not be mentioned in the study hall [as a source] for proof, because they were wicked, for they would preserve thorns in a vineyard, and according to Rabbi Eliezer they are [forbidden as] kilayim [diverse kinds]; and we do not derive a proof from them, because we did not scrutinize [their case to know] how that [deathbed] command was [given], for because they were wicked they were not mentioned in the study hall:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:2:1.hebrew: תנא קמא כר"א - דאמר שכיב מרע ובריא שוים, הלכך "הולך" דידיה לאו כ"זכי" דמי:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:2:1.english: The first Tanna [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - who says [that] a person on his deathbed and a healthy person are equal; therefore, his [saying] "deliver" is not like [saying] "acquire".

Rashi on Gittin 15a:2:2.hebrew: ויש אומרים כרבנן - דדברי שכיב מרע ככתובין וכמסורין דמי, ואפי' לא מת משלח נמי יתנו ליורשי מקבל, כל זמן שלא חזר משלח מדבריו:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:2:2.english: And "Some say" [hold] in accordance with the Rabbis - For the words of a critically ill person are [considered] as though written and handed over, and even [if] the sender has not died, they still give [it] to the heirs of the recipient, as long as the sender has not retracted his words:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:3:1.hebrew: כר"א - מדתלו טעמא במיתה, הא אם לא מת, יחזרו לו:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:3:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Elazar - Since they made the reason depend on [his] death, [it follows that] if he did not die, they return [it] to him:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:3:2.hebrew: מספקא להו - אי כר"א אי כרבנן, והיכא דמית נמי מספקא להו אי מצוה לקיים דברי המת או לא:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:3:2.english: They are uncertain - whether [the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar or in accordance with the Rabbis, and where [the giver] died as well, they are uncertain whether it is a mitzvah to fulfill the words of the dead or not.

Rashi on Gittin 15a:6:1.hebrew: תני - במילתיה דר"ש: "יחזרו למשלח", ולא תתני "ליורשי משלח", דבלא מת עסקינן:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:6:1.english: Teach - in the statement of Rabbi Shimon: "[They shall] return [it] to the sender," and do not teach "to the heirs of the sender," because we are dealing with [a case where he] has not died:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:8:1.english: One who brings [a bill of divorce, and says,] "Half of it was signed in my presence" - [This means] one of the witnesses:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:1.hebrew: א' אומר בפני נכתב ואחד אומר כו' פסול - אי כשהגט יוצא מתחת ידי האחד שהוא מביאו, ואין חבירו שליח בהבאתו, משום הכי פסול, דלשליח אצרכוה רבנן למימרינהו לתרוייהו. ולמאן דמוקי לה נמי בגמ' בששניהם שלוחים, אפ"ה פסול: כיון דחד הוא דאיכא אחתימה, ואיהו לא מסהיד אכתיבה, אתי לאיחלופי בקיום שטרות דעלמא בעד אחד, כדאמרי' בפ"ק (לעיל גיטין דף ג.):
Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:1.english: One says: It was written in my presence, and one says, etc., it is invalid - If [this refers to a case] where the get [bill of divorce] comes forth from the hand of the one [agent] who is bringing it, and his fellow is not an agent in bringing it, for that reason it is invalid, because the Rabbis required the agent to state both of them [that it was written and signed in his presence]. And also according to the one who establishes it in the Gemara [as referring to a case] where both of them are agents, even so it is invalid: since there is [only] one [witness] regarding the signing, and he does not testify regarding the writing, it could come to be confused with the ratification of ordinary documents by a single witness, as we say in the first chapter (above, Gittin, daf 3a).

Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:2.hebrew: שנים אומרים בפנינו נכתב ואחד - שלישי אומר כו', נמי פסול משום האי טעמא:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:2.english: Two say: "It was written in our presence," and one - [a] third [person] says, etc. ["It was signed in my presence"] — [it is] also invalid for this [same] reason:

Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:3.hebrew: ור' יהודה מכשיר - דכיון דמצרכינן לאסהודי נמי אכתיבה, או הוא או אחר, תו לא אתי לאיחלופי. ובגמ' אמרינן דחלוק היה ר' יהודה אף בראשונה, א"אחד אומר בפני נכתב ואחד אומר בפני נחתם":
Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:3.english: And Rabbi Yehuda deems [it] valid - For since we require testifying about the writing as well — [whether by] him or [by] another — [it] will no longer come to be confused. And in the Gemara we say that Rabbi Yehuda disagreed even regarding the first [case], regarding "One says, 'It was written in my presence,' and one says, 'It was signed in my presence'":

Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:4.hebrew: א' אומר בפני נכתב ושנים אומרים בפנינו נחתם כשר - בגמ' מפרש לה:
Rashi on Gittin 15a:9:4.english: One says, "It was written in my presence," and two say, "It was signed in our presence," [it is] valid - it is explained in the Gemara:

Tosafot on Gittin 15a:13:1.hebrew: או כולו בקיום הגט כו' - לפי מה דבעי למימר בפ"ק (לעיל גיטין דף ו.), גבי רב חסדא מצריך מאקטיספון לארדשיר, דקסבר לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה, איכא למימר דהכא איירי בשנים מעידים על חתימת השני, דנעשה לשמה:
Tosafot on Gittin 15a:13:1.english: Either entirely through the ratification of a bill of divorce, etc. - According to what [the Gemara] seeks to say in the first chapter (above, Gittin 6a), regarding Rav Ḥisda, [who] requires [the declaration] from Aktisfon to Ardashir because he holds [that it is] because they are not expert in [writing a bill of divorce] for her sake, one can say that here it is speaking of two [witnesses] testifying about the signature of the second [witness], that it was done for her sake:

Tosafot on Gittin 15a:13:2.hebrew: או כולו בתקנת חכמים - קסבר דלא דייק השליח כל כך כשאין כל העדות מתקיימת על ידו, ורבא סבר דמ"מ דייק שפיר:
Tosafot on Gittin 15a:13:2.english: Or [it must be] entirely via the rabbinic decree - [Rav Ḥisda] holds that the agent is not so careful when not all of the testimony is established through him, whereas Rava holds that nevertheless he is properly careful:

Tosafot on Gittin 15a:3:1.hebrew: ורבי יהודה הנשיא כו' כר"א והיכא דמת אמרינן מצוה לקיים כו' - פירוש: היכא דמת נותן קודם שמת המקבל, אבל דברי שכיב מרע כמסורין דמו, אפילו מת מקבל ברישא, כדפירשנו לעיל:
Tosafot on Gittin 15a:3:1.english: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, etc., in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, and where [the giver] died we say it is a mitzva to fulfill, etc. - Meaning: [this applies] where the giver died before the recipient died; however, the words of a dying person are considered as if [already] handed over, even if the recipient died first, as we explained above:

Tosafot on Gittin 15a:4:1.hebrew: או דקאמר משמיה דנשיא - לפי שלא מצינו שהיה נשיא, קבעי: שמא חיסר התנא מדבריו, והיה לו לשנות "אמר ר"ש: הנשיא אומר". ופשיט מרב יוסף, ודחי: עדיין תבעי — הנשיא אומר, או דקאמר משמיה דנשיא — דשמא לישנא דברייתא נקט רב יוסף. ומצינו שהתנא שונה כענין זה בב"ק (דף לט:): "ר' יעקב משלם חצי נזק", ופריך: "ר' יעקב מאי עבידתיה":
Tosafot on Gittin 15a:4:1.english: Or that he spoke in the name of the Nasi - Since we have not found that [Rabbi Shimon] was a Nasi, [the Gemara] asks: perhaps the Tanna omitted [a word] from his statement, and he should have taught, "Rabbi Shimon said: The Nasi says." And [the Gemara] resolves [it] from Rav Yosef, and [then] rejects [this proof]: You can still ask [whether it means] "the Nasi says," or that he spoke in the name of the Nasi, for perhaps Rav Yosef [merely] used the phrasing of the baraita. And we find that the Tanna teaches in a similar manner in Bava Kamma (39b): "Rabbi Yaakov pays half-damages," and [the Gemara] asks: "What is Rabbi Yaakov doing [here]?":

Tosafot on Gittin 15a:6:2.hebrew: המביא. בפני נכתב כולו ובפני נחתם חציו - בגמ' משמע דגרסי' ברישא "בפני נחתם כולו, בפני נכתב חציו". ותימה למ"ד "לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו": כיון דתנא "בפני נכתב חציו ונחתם כולו" פסול, כ"ש "בפני נחתם חציו"! ואומר ר"י דאיצטריך, דסד"א ליתכשר, דחשיב טפי מכתב סופר ועד, דאיכא שני עדים חתומין, אלא דליכא קיום אלא אכתיבה וחתימת עד אחד; ועדיף מ"בפני נחתם כולו ונכתב חציו", דבעינן שיעיד על עיקר כתיבה, כדאמרי' בריש מכילתא (דף ג.): דלמא אתי לאיחלופי בקיום שטרות דעלמא:
Tosafot on Gittin 15a:6:2.english: One who brings [a get]. In my presence all of it was written, and in my presence half of it was signed - In the Gemara it is implied that we read at the beginning [of the Mishnah]: "In my presence all of it was signed, in my presence half of it was written." And this is puzzling according to the one who says [the reason for the declaration is] "because witnesses are not readily available to uphold it": since [the Mishnah] taught [that if he says] "In my presence half of it was written and all of it was signed" it is invalid, all the more so [when he says] "In my presence half of it was signed" [and all of it was written, it should be invalid]! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it was necessary [to teach it], for you might have thought that it should be valid, since it is considered better than [a get with] the writing of a scribe and one witness — for [here] there are two witnesses signed, except that there is no confirmation except for the writing and the signature of one witness; and it is better than "In my presence all of it was signed and half of it was written," where we require that he testify about the main writing, as we say at the beginning of the tractate (3a): lest it come to be confused with the confirmation of ordinary documents:
